subject: Security questionnaire: hosted API residency, retention & deletion clarifications for DataFirm
messages:
From: Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@datafirm.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@datafirm.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API security questionnaire - residency & retention questions

Hi Connor,

Thanks for taking this. Our security team is working through the hosted API section of our vendor questionnaire and we have a few items where we need clarified answers for legal review. Can you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted inference offering?

1) Data residency: where customer request payloads, generated responses, metadata, and derived artifacts (embeddings, reranks) are persisted by default? Are there region options (US, EU) and how is region selection enforced?

2) Retention windows: what are the default retention periods for (a) raw requests & responses, (b) embeddings/derived artifacts, (c) audit logs and traces, and (d) backups/snapshots? Are there configurable retention controls per-account?

3) Deletion: what is the deletion process? If a customer requests deletion, what exactly is removed (primary storage, caches, backups), and what is the SLA for full deletion? Are there APIs we can call to programmatically delete data?

4) Backups & disaster recovery: where are encrypted backups stored, what is their retention, and how are they handled for cross-region replication?

5) Third-party processors & encryption: list major subprocessors and confirm in-transit and at-rest encryption; confirm if customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) are supported on hosted API.

I've attached our questionnaire extract with the specific fields (security_questionnaire_v1.docx). If you can provide a concise written response we can attach to our security review, that would be great.

Best,
Anna
Anna Ruiz
Security Analyst, DataFirm Inc

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. I'm copying Evelyn from Security so you get definitive answers for the items below; I put a short summary here and Evelyn has expanded details in her follow-up.

Short answers (summary):
- Data residency: Default hosted region is US (multi-az). EU-hosted tenancy is available on request for enterprise contracts; region selection enforced at account provisioning time and backed by regional storage and routing.
- Retention: default operational retention for raw request/response content is 14 days; derived artifacts (embeddings/feature vectors) retained 180 days by default; audit logs retained 365 days. We offer per-account retention settings for enterprise plans.
- Deletion: customers can request deletion via the Console or API; standard deletion SLA for hosted accounts is 72 hours to remove live data and caches, with up to 7 days for snapshot pruning.
- Backups: encrypted snapshots are stored in-region and retained for 90 days by default; cross-region replication is only enabled for Dedicated/Private solutions unless contracted.
- Encryption & subprocessors: in-transit TLS 1.2+ and at-rest AES-256. We support KMS integration for Dedicated/Private; hosted customers may request CMEK on an enterprise contract — Evelyn notes limitations below. Major subprocessors: AWS (S3/EBS), Cloud Monitoring provider (scrubbed), and a managed logging vendor.

Attachments I will provide: SOC2 summary and a simple hosted-data flow diagram (attached in next email). If you need formal wording for your questionnaire, Evelyn's message is suitable to paste into the doc. Happy to hop on a call if you prefer.

Thanks,

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@datafirm.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API security questionnaire - residency & retention questions

Hi Anna — thanks for the follow-ups. Below are definitive answers you can paste into your questionnaire. I've included operational notes and references to APIs where applicable.

1) Data residency (hosted API)
- Default behaviour: customer request payloads, generated responses, request metadata, and derived artifacts are stored in the region associated with the customer's hosted tenancy. For self-service hosted accounts the default region is US (us-west-2 primary); EU tenancy (eu-west-1) is available and must be requested at account setup or via an enterprise onboarding order. Region assignment is enforced at provisioning and by our smart routing layer; ingress endpoints are region-aware and cross-region routing of customer data is prevented for EU-tenanted accounts.
- Note: Dedicated and Private deployments provide stronger guarantees and are recommended for customers with strict data residency regulations.

2) Retention windows (default hosted settings)
- Raw requests & responses (request payloads, model outputs): retained for 14 days by default to support debugging, rate-limiting, and abuse detection. Customers on enterprise plans may request custom retention policies (minimum 0 days) as part of the contract.
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, reranks, fingerprint hashes): retained 180 days by default; customers may opt-out of storing derived artifacts by enabling the "no-persist" flag at the API call or via account settings (enterprise).
- Audit logs & traces (control plane operations, admin changes): retained 365 days and stored as immutable audit records. The audit record contains action metadata (who/when) but does not include full request/response payloads.
- Backups & snapshots: encrypted snapshots are retained for 90 days by default. Snapshots are created for DR and are stored in-region; cross-region snapshot replication is only available for Dedicated/Private with a contractual add-on.

3) Deletion process and SLA
- Live data & caches: when a deletion request is submitted via the Console or the Data Deletion API (DELETE /v1/accounts/{account_id}/data), a deletion job is queued that removes entries from primary storage and invalidates KV/prefix caches. Cache invalidation removes all keys associated with the account and prevents future reads.
- Backups & snapshots: snapshot removal is scheduled as a background operation. While a snapshot may be immutable for a short retention window, the snapshot lifecycle manager will remove any retained snapshot containing the customer's data within the configured snapshot retention SLA. By default, full purge from snapshots completes within 7 days of the deletion request; customers requiring an accelerated purge can negotiate a shorter window in the contract.
- Audit trail: all deletion requests generate an immutable audit record capturing the requestor identity, timestamp, scope of deletion, and the resulting job id. The audit record references job ids and metadata only — it does NOT include deleted request/response payloads. Audit records are retained for compliance and eDiscovery per the audit retention window.
- SLA: standard hosted deletion SLA is 72 hours for live data & cache removal, and up to 7 days for snapshot pruning (contractual exceptions possible). We will provide a deletion confirmation receipt with job id upon completion.

4) Backups & disaster recovery
- Encrypted snapshots are taken regularly and stored in-region with AES-256 encryption. Snapshot keys are managed by the cloud provider; for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed keys (CMEK) and HSM integrations. For hosted customers, CMEK is available on an enterprise agreement.
- Cross-region replication is not enabled by default for hosted customers; it is part of the Dedicated/Private offering or can be enabled via an add-on.

5) Subprocessors & encryption
- Major subprocessors: AWS (EC2, S3, EBS), StackMonitor Inc. (metrics), ManagedLogCo (log aggregation). We provide standard subprocessors' information in our vendor list and update it quarterly.
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest. KMS/CMEK support is available for Dedicated/Private and can be enabled for hosted on request under an enterprise contract.

6) Legal hold & eDiscovery
- Redwood supports customer-requested legal holds. Legal hold requests should be made through your account representative and will prevent deletion actions for the specified scope until the hold is released by an authorized customer admin. Legal holds are recorded in the audit trail. Note that legal hold requests may affect retention billing and are processed in accordance with our legal and compliance policies.

Operational notes / APIs you can reference in the questionnaire:
- Data Deletion API: DELETE /v1/accounts/{account_id}/data (deletes live data and invalidates caches; returns job id)
- Deletion status: GET /v1/jobs/{job_id} (returns progress and final status)
- Retention settings: GET/PUT /v1/accounts/{account_id}/retention (enterprise-only to set custom windows)

If helpful, I've attached a short SOC2 summary and a hosted data-flow image that maps where artifacts live in-region.

Please tell me if you need contract phrasing (we can provide standard exhibit language for retention and legal hold).

Regards,
